# BSPAmbientLight

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [BSP](Blitz3D-BSP)

</div>


```blitzbasic
BSPAmbientLight:Void bsp:Int32, red:Float32, green:Float32, blue:Float32
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bsp` | In | Int32 | required | The level. |
| `red` | In | Float32 | required | Red part, 0 to 255. |
| `green` | In | Float32 | required | Green part, 0 to 255. |
| `blue` | In | Float32 | required | Blue part, 0 to 255. |

## Description

Sets the ambient light of a level, a color that is added to the light the level has, which is its lightmap or, with vertex lighting, the colors of its vertices. A new level starts at 0, 0, 0, so nothing is added. Levels ignore the normal [AmbientLight](AmbientLight), which is why this command exists. It can make a dark level easier to see, although using the gamma value of [LoadBSP](LoadBSP) looks nicer in the original. To multiply the level with a color instead, use [BSPLightmapColor](BSPLightmapColor).

## Differences

* The original also lights the vertices of a level with point and spot lights, which have no effect on a level here. The color is not changed by [BSPLightmapColor](BSPLightmapColor).
